name: Uzzah and the ark
summary: The ark had been taken by the Philistines in the days of the judges and had rested in the house of Abinadab. David gathered thirty thousand chosen men to bring it up, and they set it upon a new cart driven by Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab. At Nachon's threshingfloor the oxen shook the cart, Uzzah put forth his hand and took hold of the ark, and God smote him there for his error, and he died by the ark.
offense: David and the congregation agreed to bring the ark up from the house of Abinadab. They placed it upon a new cart, and music and rejoicing accompanied the journey (2 Samuel 6:1-5). The purpose was welcome to the people, but the manner of carrying the ark had already been commanded. Approval by an assembly did not replace the Lord's due order. Numbers 4:15 required the holy things to be covered before the appointed bearers approached and forbade them to touch them lest they die. The ark's staves were to remain in their rings (Exodus 25:14-15). The Philistines had returned it upon a cart, but Israel was responsible for the instruction given to Israel. A new vehicle was not an improvement upon obedience. At the threshingfloor the oxen shook it, and Uzzah put out his hand to hold the ark (2 Samuel 6:6). His reach answered an immediate danger, but it crossed a boundary the law had not left to personal judgment. Even Aaron was forbidden to enter the holy place at all times, a warning given after the deaths of his sons (Leviticus 16:1-2). Nearness to holy service required greater care, not freedom from its limits.
judgment: The Lord's anger was kindled against Uzzah, and he died there beside the ark. David was displeased at the breach and afraid, asking how the ark could come to him (2 Samuel 6:7-9). The celebration was stopped by a judgment that made the neglected command impossible to dismiss. Psalms 119:120 joins trembling in the flesh to fear of the Lord's judgments. The ark remained three months in Obed-edom's house. When David returned to bring it up, he did not merely try the same journey with more confidence. He declared that none but the Levites ought to carry it, called them to sanctify themselves, and acknowledged that the first breach came because they had not sought the Lord after the due order (1 Chronicles 15:2, 12-13). The failure was confessed as theirs, not assigned to Uzzah alone. The Levites then bore the ark upon their shoulders with the staves as Moses had commanded (1 Chronicles 15:14-15). Rejoicing continued, but now the service followed the word. The distinction between the journeys was not whether David wanted to honour the Lord. It was whether that honour was offered in the manner the Lord had appointed.

verses.text: And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab that was in Gibeah: and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drave the new cart.
And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab which was at Gibeah, accompanying the ark of God: and Ahio went before the ark.
And David and all the house of Israel played before the Lord on all manner of instruments made of fir wood, even on harps, and on psalteries, and on timbrels, and on cornets, and on cymbals.
And when they came to Nachon’s threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook it.
And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.

And when Aaron and his sons have made an end of covering the sanctuary, and all the vessels of the sanctuary, as the camp is to set forward; after that, the sons of Kohath shall come to bear it: but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. These things are the burden of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the congregation.
For because ye did it not at the first, the Lord our God made a breach upon us, for that we sought him not after the due order.
So the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of the Lord God of Israel.
And the children of the Levites bare the ark of God upon their shoulders with the staves thereon, as Moses commanded according to the word of the Lord.

entries.commentary: David gathered together thirty thousand chosen men of Israel. Not everyone is a warrior, and not everyone goes to the front lines, but everyone in the body is important in some way; the members that seem more feeble are needful, and on them more honor is bestowed. David and all the people went from Baale of Judah to bring up the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the Lord of hosts that dwelleth between the cherubims. The ark had been taken from Israel by the Philistines in the days of the judges because of sin, and it had been left in the house of Abinadab. Through the wilderness there had been no house for the Lord, so the ark was moved from place to place. They set the ark upon a new cart, and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove it, with Ahio going before the ark, while David and all the house of Israel played before the Lord on harps, psalteries, timbrels, cornets, and cymbals.

When they came to Nachon's threshingfloor, the oxen shook the cart, and Uzzah put forth his hand and took hold of the ark. The anger of the Lord was kindled, and God smote him for his error, and he died there by the ark. Only chosen men could come near the ark. The Lord had warned Aaron not to come at all times into the holy place before the mercy seat that he die not, and had set many stipulations upon it, even after the two sons of Aaron died for offering strange fire. The Most High is holy and not to be handled carelessly. Grabbing the ark was a natural reaction, but the Most High had already declared it holy and untouchable. Everything in that day had to be done to a T; we owe thanks that there is mercy through Christ, for the Lord was not playing about His commandments. David was displeased that the Lord had made a breach upon Uzzah, and he was afraid of the Lord that day, saying, How shall the ark of the Lord come to me? David had seen the power of the Lord, and his flesh trembled for fear of Him and His judgments. David would not remove the ark to the city of David but carried it aside to the house of Obededom the Gittite, where it remained three months; and the Lord blessed Obededom and all his household because of the ark.

When David heard the Lord had blessed the house of Obededom because of the ark, he went and brought up the ark to the city of David with gladness. When those that bore it had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings. David danced before the Lord with all his might, girded with a linen ephod. He was happy and in the spirit, for the Lord had chosen him to bring the ark back among the people. Israel brought up the ark with shouting and the sound of the trumpet. Michal, Saul's daughter, looked through a window and saw David leaping and dancing before the Lord, and she despised him in her heart. This is a spirit to be careful of: coming out of the spirit on the Lord's day and murmuring against a brother who is rejoicing in the Most High. David set the ark in the tabernacle he had pitched for it, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts. He dealt to every one, both men and women, a cake of bread, a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine, and the people departed to their houses.

David returned to bless his own household, still in a good mood. Michal came out to meet him and said sarcastically, How glorious was the king of Israel today, who uncovered himself in the eyes of the handmaids as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself. She had watched from a distance and could think only of the king dancing with his clothes falling, when the Most High had just brought the ark of God back among Israel. She forgot the greatness of the day and let a murmuring spirit take her. David answered that he danced before the Lord who chose him before her father to be ruler over Israel, therefore he would play before the Lord, and would yet be more vile and base in his own sight, and of the maidservants he would be had in honor. Michal, the daughter of Saul, had no child unto the day of her death; the Lord shut her womb. Do not play with the Most High.

The sons of Kohath were numbered from thirty years old and upward even unto fifty years old, all that enter into the host to do the work in the tabernacle of the congregation. You took on that responsibility at thirty years old. Fifty was basically the age of retirement from the service; the law elsewhere shows the elder then sat down to be a judge amongst his brethren.

This is the service of the sons of Kohath about the most holy things. When the camp set forward, Aaron and his sons took down the covering vail and covered the ark of the testimony with it, with the covering of badgers' skins and a cloth wholly of blue. The design of the ark and the tabernacle, the pure gold dishes, spoons, and vessels, was laid out back in [Exodus 35](/bible/exodus/35) and 36; review it there.

The table of shewbread, the candlestick, the golden altar, and all the instruments of ministry were each wrapped in cloths of blue, scarlet, or purple and covered with badgers' skins before they were put on the staves and bars. Badger skin is something we would consider unclean today, yet the Lord had his holy things covered in it. Under the law of sacrifice, defilement came by touching unclean things to eat them; touching them to make something for the tabernacle still left you unclean until sundown, unable to sacrifice, but the skins themselves served the sanctuary.

After Aaron and his sons made an end of covering the sanctuary, the sons of Kohath came to bear it, but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. The Most High is very particular about the most holy things. The Lord referred to all the tribes together as the camp. If you are not in a camp you are out of order; people avoid camps because a camp carries a certain level of order and subjection, and they want to do their own thing, which is to sit in the midst of sin. All twelve tribes are not gathered together right now, but we are still commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, and that takes gathering; the body must move in one unison, in one direction, as a camp.

To the office of Eleazar pertained the oil for the light, the sweet incense, the daily meat offering, the anointing oil, and the oversight of all the tabernacle. The burning of the sweet incense stayed in that priestly line: Zacharias, of the course of Abia, descended from the line of the Kohathites, and his lot was to burn incense in the temple of the Lord. [Luke 1:6](/bible/luke/1#v6) is the New Testament precept for what it means to be righteous: walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. Highlight that and commit it to memory. The son of Zacharias was John the Baptist, a Levite; and John the Baptist was Elijah back on the earth again, come to do what was prophesied of him. There is no reincarnation, coming back as a bird or such; there is regeneration, and we come back over and over again.

The Most High commanded that the families of the Kohathites not be cut off: Aaron and his sons appointed every one to his service and to his burden, but they shall not go in to see when the holy things are covered, lest they die. It was a heavy responsibility; your life was on the line and you could not be out of order. One slip, one curious peek at the shiny gold before it was covered, and God put you to death on the spot. You had to be serious about your job and follow all instructions. That is the God we are dealing with; that is why Christ came, to give us mercy and grace from that thing.

The sons of Gershon were numbered from thirty to fifty years old for their service: bearing the curtains of the tabernacle, the coverings of badgers' skins, the hangings of the court and the doors, the cords, and all the instruments of their service. Their charge was under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. Ithamar had to make sure the priests had covered all the most holy things before the Gershonites came in to bear them; he was responsible for the lives of all the Gershonites that served, and he had to be in order.

The sons of Merari were numbered from thirty to fifty years old, charged with the boards, bars, pillars, sockets, pins, and cords of the tabernacle and the court, reckoned by name, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron. Only Eleazar and Ithamar were left to oversee, because Nadab and Abihu were killed by the Lord for offering strange fire; there were only two sons of Aaron remaining.

The numbered for service were 2,750 Kohathites, 2,630 Gershonites, and 3,200 Merarites; the total of those from thirty to fifty years old that entered the service of the tabernacle was 8,580, eight thousand and five hundred and fourscore. The Lord constantly repeats himself through these chapters to make sure you stay in order and do not go out of order, because going out of order cost your life. That is why you read the same thing in the Bible over and over again.

David prepared a place and pitched a tent for the ark in the city of David. He declared that none ought to carry the ark but the Levites, for the Most High had chosen them to carry it and to minister unto him forever. -

David assembled all Israel and the chief Levites by their families, naming the sons of Kohath, Merari, Gershom, Elizaphan, Hebron, and Uzziel with their chiefs and numbers. He called for the priests Zadok and Abiathar and for the Levites, showing the Most High had set a clear structure among the priesthood.

David charged the chief fathers of the Levites to sanctify themselves before bringing up the ark, because the first attempt failed when they did not seek him after the due order. The Levites bore the ark upon their shoulders with the staves, as Moses commanded according to the word of the Most High. -

David appointed Levites as singers with psalteries, harps, and cymbals, to lift up the voice with joy. Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were appointed to sound cymbals of brass; others played harps and psalteries; the priests blew the trumpets before the ark, and doorkeepers were set. Every rank had its assigned place.

David and the elders and captains went to bring up the ark from the house of Obededom with joy. When the Most High helped the Levites bearing the ark, they offered seven bullocks and seven rams. David was clothed in a robe of fine linen along with the Levites and singers, and wore an ephod of linen. The people were dressed well, and the same custom carried down through Solomon.

All Israel brought up the ark with shouting, cornet, trumpets, cymbals, psalteries, and harps. Michal the daughter of Saul looked out the window and despised David in her heart as he danced and played. In the midst of pure righteousness she was out of the spirit, hating him instead of rejoicing.
